content: Tumor infiltrating stromal reaction refers to the changes in the non-cancerous connective tissue (stroma) surrounding a tumor. When a tumor forms, the surrounding stroma often reacts or changes in response to the presence of cancer cells. This reaction can include an increase in the number of cells, changes in cell type, like increased fibroblasts or immune cells, or changes in proteins, vasculature, and extracellular matrix components. The characteristics of this stromal reaction can influence the behavior of the cancer, including its ability to grow, invade surrounding tissues, and metastasize to other parts of the body. It's an area of great interest in the field of cancer research.
